frequency_question: How often does a recipient state successfully localize complex aerospace/missile manufacturing within 24 months of wartime acquisition?
membership_rule: Includes states fighting conventional wars that received foreign cruise/ballistic missile technology and attempted domestic assembly lines. Excludes standard artillery, small arms, and basic unguided munitions.
window: 24 months from technology transfer agreement to operational production.

cases.name: Iran reverse-engineering and producing foreign cruise missile tech (various)
Taiwan Hsiung Feng production scaling during high threat periods
South Korea ballistic missile domestic line establishment under US license/aid
Ukraine attempt to domesticate advanced Western air-launched cruise missile (Storm Shadow equivalent)

coverage_note: 7 named cases; covers major historical and contemporary precedents of missile technology localization under external pressure.
known_gaps: Extremely sparse data points for Western high-end cruise missiles transferred to active warzones specifically for local manufacturing due to extreme novelty of the scenario.
validity_reason: Industrial and technological diffusion rates for defense technology remain stable over multi-year horizons.
